hero.headline: Senate passes $69.5 billion immigration enforcement funding package
hero.body:
The Senate voted early Friday morning to pass a $69.5 billion budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement operations through 2029. The legislation passed 52-47 following an overnight session that included contentious debates over amendments.

The bill represents a significant expansion of resources for immigration enforcement and border security operations over the next three years. The measure now moves to the House for final passage before President Donald Trump can sign it into law.

The contentious debate centered on a proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund that the Trump administration intends to create to compensate political allies who claim they were prosecuted by the Biden-era Justice Department. Several Republicans objected to the fund and worked to block it through amendments.

During the marathon voting session, six Republican senators broke ranks with their party to support an amendment sponsored by Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana designed to block the fund. Those senators included Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Dan Sullivan of Alaska, and Joni Ernst of Iowa.

Cassidy spent considerable time during the overnight session perfecting the language of his amendment to prevent the administration from establishing the compensation fund. He consulted with Senate Parliamentarian Elizabeth MacDonough to ensure the amendment could withstand procedural challenges.

The division revealed internal Republican disagreements over spending priorities and the anti-weaponization fund, yet party leadership maintained sufficient support for passage. Despite the splits, Republicans held together enough votes to pass the measure without Democratic support.

The funding package comes amid broader debates over immigration enforcement and departmental operations. Democrats had previously blocked a separate Department of Homeland Security funding bill, demanding reforms to Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. Those proposed changes included requirements that agents wear identification and body cameras, as well as restrictions preventing them from operating near schools, medical facilities, churches, polling stations, childcare facilities, and courts.

Democrats also sought guarantees that local and state law enforcement agencies could investigate potential crimes committed by federal authorities, including excessive use of force. Republicans supported body cameras but resisted other proposals, arguing they would restrict agents' ability to conduct operations effectively.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer stated his party wanted "commonsense" changes in how immigration enforcement operates. "From day one, I've said unless there were really strong, meaningful reforms to rein in ICE and stop the violence, there will not be Democratic votes to fund ICE," Schumer said.

Republican leaders expressed confidence the House will pass the measure in coming days. The bill's passage represents a victory for Republican leadership despite the internal tensions revealed during the overnight voting marathon and amendments debate.

cards.headline: Zelensky Proposes Direct Talks With Putin to End War
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent an open letter to Russia's leader calling for face-to-face negotiations as US attention shifts to Iran.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has written an open letter directly to Putin, marking the first public letter he has addressed to the Russian leader since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. In the letter, Zelensky calls for face-to-face negotiations and argues that only direct engagement between Ukraine and Russia can end the war.

Zelensky has proposed meeting in a neutral third country. The public letter includes a sweeping critique of Putin's 26 years in power. The diplomatic overture comes as Trump has stated that both sides will need to make compromises to resolve the conflict.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Lebanon-Israel Ceasefire Proposal
cards.teaser: The group turned down a truce plan as Israeli strikes in Lebanon continued and uncertainty surrounded US-Iran negotiations.
cards.body:
Hezbollah has rejected a ceasefire agreement between Lebanon and Israel that was announced by the United States following fresh diplomatic talks. The rejection came as Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon persisted.

The rejection also occurred amid a UN peacekeeping incident in southeastern Lebanon, where a UNIFIL peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded by mortar fire. The situation underscores the ongoing tensions in the region despite diplomatic efforts to establish a ceasefire.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping to Visit North Korea Next Week in First Trip Since 2019
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week, marking his first visit to the country since 2019. The trip comes at a time when regional dynamics have shifted considerably, with North Korea strengthening its ties with Moscow in recent years.

The visit will bring Xi together with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un weeks after Xi held separate discussions with the leaders of both the United States and Russia, two countries that play significant roles in North Korea's foreign policy calculations.

China has historically served as North Korea's main economic and diplomatic supporter, providing crucial trade and political backing at international forums. However, North Korea's growing alignment with Russia has introduced new complexity to Beijing's traditional role as Pyongyang's primary benefactor. The strengthened Russia-North Korea relationship has given Kim Jong Un alternative sources of support and reduced his historical dependence on China.

Beijing has long viewed stability on the Korean Peninsula as crucial to its own security interests. This visit reflects China's continued commitment to maintaining its relationship with North Korea despite the shifting geopolitical landscape. The timing also comes amid broader regional tensions, with the United States maintaining a significant military presence in South Korea and Japan.

The meeting between Xi and Kim will be closely watched by regional observers and global powers. As one analysis noted, Xi faces "an emboldened North Korean dictator, whose alliance with Russia has reduced his dependence on China." How the two leaders navigate their relationship in light of North Korea's expanded ties with Russia could signal important shifts in the balance of power in East Asia.

The visit represents a significant diplomatic engagement at a time when multiple conflicts and tensions are reshaping international alignments. North Korea has taken steps to consolidate its relationship with Russia, which has altered traditional power dynamics in the region. Meanwhile, China continues to balance its interests in maintaining influence over North Korea while managing its own relationships with other major powers.

The trip underscores the delicate diplomatic situation in northeast Asia, where historical relationships are being tested by new geopolitical realities. For China, the visit offers an opportunity to reinforce its position as a key player in regional stability, even as North Korea pursues a more independent foreign policy path. The outcomes of Xi and Kim's discussions could have implications for how regional tensions develop in the coming months and years.

cards.headline: Trump directs $700 million to coal industry under wartime powers
cards.body:
President Trump has announced federal support for the coal industry through multiple executive actions, framing the investments as necessary to strengthen domestic energy production and security.

During a White House ceremony, Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of Defense to purchase long-term power from coal plants serving military installations and other mission-critical facilities. "We're going to be buying a lot of coal through the military now," Trump said at the event, which included coal executives, miners, and administration officials including EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Interior Secretary Doug Burgess.

The Peabody Energy CEO James Grech presented Trump with an award from the Washington Coal Club during the ceremony. "We stand here today representing the thousands of coalminers across the country to express our deep gratitude to you, sir, for the actions you've taken to support our industry," Grech said.

Beyond the military purchasing agreement, Trump announced that the Department of Energy would allocate $175 million to six projects designed to upgrade and extend the lifespan of coal-fired power plants serving rural and remote communities in West Virginia, Ohio, North Carolina and Kentucky.

Trump framed the initiative within a broader energy agenda. "Under our leadership, we're becoming a massive energy exporter. We're lifting up our hard-working American miners like nobody has ever done before," he stated.

This action represents the latest administration effort to revive the struggling coal sector. In September, the White House announced it would open 13.1 million acres of public land to coal mining and provide $625 million for coal-fired power plants.

The coal industry has faced sustained decline over the past three decades. According to the Energy Information Administration, US coal production in 2023 was less than half its 2008 level. Coal plants generated only about 15 percent of US electricity in 2024, down from roughly 50 percent in 2000, as utilities have shifted toward natural gas and renewable energy sources.

The administration's coal investments come amid rising energy prices following military operations against Iran. The timing reflects broader administration priorities, with Trump receiving various gifts and honors from business leaders since taking office. In recent months, the president has granted business exemptions and trade considerations following such presentations.

The executive orders demonstrate Trump's willingness to use presidential authority to support industries aligned with his economic agenda, particularly sectors facing market pressures. The coal investments signal an administration commitment to domestic fossil fuel production despite the industry's long-term decline in US electricity generation.

cards.headline: House Armed Services Committee advances $1.15 trillion defense bill
cards.teaser: The committee passed the annual defense policy bill after debating hundreds of amendments for 14 hours.
cards.body:
The House Armed Services Committee approved the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act on Thursday, advancing the $1.15 trillion defense policy bill to the full House for consideration.

The committee voted 44 in favor of the measure after spending 14 hours debating approximately 900 proposed amendments. The annual defense authorization bill now awaits action by the full chamber.

cards.headline: House Passes Ukraine Aid Over Republican Leadership Opposition
cards.teaser: Eighteen Republican lawmakers joined Democrats to approve assistance for Ukraine in a rebuke to the president's foreign policy.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives passed legislation to aid Ukraine and impose sanctions on key segments of the Russian economy in a 226-195 vote, defying Republican leadership opposition. The vote marks the chamber's second major foreign policy break with the Trump administration in a week, following a war powers resolution on Iran the previous day.

Republican leaders had argued the bill would undermine ongoing negotiations, but the bipartisan coalition moved forward regardless. The passage reflects growing House impatience with the administration's approach to the Ukraine conflict.

cards.headline: Ex-Wife of Dubai Ruler's Nephew Reported in Custody
cards.teaser: Prosecutors said Zeynab Javadli has been in custody after losing contact with friends earlier this week.
cards.body:
Zeynab Javadli, the former wife of a nephew of Dubai's ruler, is in custody according to prosecutors. Javadli had not been in contact with any of her friends since Tuesday.

The announcement by prosecutors came after concerns arose about her whereabouts when she stopped communicating with her social circle. No further information about the circumstances of her custody has been provided.

cards.headline: Missing Sherpa Guide Found Alive on Everest After Week-Long Search
cards.teaser: Hillary Dawa Sherpa was discovered crawling toward base camp after surviving six days alone on the mountain.
cards.body:
A Sherpa guide who went missing on Mount Everest was found alive after six days alone on the mountain. Cleaners spotted Dawa Sherpa crawling toward Base Camp as he made his way down from a higher altitude.

The rescue came as a remarkable turn of events, as funeral rites had already begun based on assumptions he had not survived. Climber Chris Thrall was with Sherpa when they lost contact, marking the beginning of his solitary struggle in the harsh mountain conditions before he was discovered by the cleaning crew.

cards.headline: Australian Authorities Seize 100,000 Illegal Cockroaches in Record Bust
cards.teaser: Prosecutors described the case as involving a cockroach kingpin in what authorities called an unprecedented insect smuggling operation.
cards.body:
Australian authorities conducted what they described as a record bug bust, seizing 100,000 illegal cockroaches. The operation targeted what prosecutors called a cockroach kingpin involved in the illegal insect trade.

The case represents one of the largest seizures of smuggled insects in Australian history. Authorities provided no additional information about the purpose of the illegal cockroach operation or how the insects were being transported.

hero.headline: John Bolton pleads guilty to mishandling classified information
hero.body:
John Bolton, former national security adviser under President Donald Trump, has reached a plea agreement in federal court on charges of mishandling classified documents. Under the agreement, which is subject to court approval, Bolton will plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information.

As part of the plea deal, Bolton must pay a $2.25 million fine. The sentencing guidelines allow for anywhere between no prison time and five years, though final sentencing will be determined by the court. Bolton is scheduled to appear in court on June 26 to formally enter his guilty plea.

The Justice Department filed the criminal charges against Bolton in October 2025. The case centers on notes and diary entries Bolton created during his tenure as national security adviser from April 2018 to September 2019. Prosecutors alleged he maintained classified materials on a computer in his Bethesda, Maryland home and in his Washington DC office from April 2018 through August 2025. Materials recovered during an August raid included briefings about weapons of mass destruction and intelligence related to foreign adversaries' leadership and foreign policy matters.

Bolton's legal team, led by attorney Abbe Lowell, has characterized the case as politically motivated. Lowell argued that the notes were personal memoirs rather than officially classified documents. The defense points to the timing of the prosecution and charges against other Trump critics, including former FBI director James Comey and New York attorney general Letitia James, as evidence of political targeting.

Bolton's legal troubles stem partly from his 2020 memoir, "The Room Where It Happened," which offered a critical behind-the-scenes account of his time in the Trump administration. The Justice Department initially sought to block the book's publication on national security grounds through a civil complaint in June 2020. The FBI subsequently investigated Bolton during the Biden administration regarding both the memoir and a 2021 foreign hack of his personal email.

Bolton left the Trump administration in September 2019 and later became a vocal critic of the former president. Trump has dismissed Bolton as a "bad guy," claiming he was unaware of the criminal charges filed against him.

The case reflects broader government efforts to enforce stricter protocols around classified information handling among senior officials. It also comes as Bolton's foreign policy predictions about Trump's second term have proven prescient, with the former adviser noting that more than half the world's countries currently lack US ambassadors and American foreign relationships have taken a backseat to Trump's personal priorities.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans work through night on ICE funding bill
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans held overnight sessions in an effort to pass funding for immigration enforcement.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans worked through the night in an attempt to advance funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The overnight legislative session reflects the urgency Republicans have placed on immigration enforcement funding.

The push for ICE funding comes as the Trump administration advances its immigration agenda. Some lawmakers are facing tests of how far they will support various elements of the president's policy priorities.

cards.headline: Senate rejects effort to block Trump payout fund
cards.teaser: Republicans defeated an attempt to bar a controversial $1.8 billion fund intended to compensate those alleging government overreach.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans narrowly defeated a Democratic attempt to block creation of a $1.8 billion fund that would allow Trump to compensate allies claiming they were targets of government weaponization. Democratic leader Chuck Schumer had proposed adding language to bar the payouts to Republican-backed legislation funding Trump's mass deportation campaign.

The narrow vote exposed divisions within the Republican Party, with some GOP senators joining Democrats in opposing the fund. The proposal has drawn criticism over its potential for abuse, particularly concerns that it could issue settlements to people connected to January 6.

cards.headline: Auburn student missing in Japan for over a week
cards.teaser: An Alabama college student has been missing in Kyoto for more than a week after separating from his family during a vacation.
cards.body:
An Auburn University student has been missing in Kyoto, Japan, for over a week after last being seen by his family. His parents say he went off alone following a disagreement during their family vacation.

The family has made public pleas for help locating their son, and the Alabama community has organized prayer gatherings as the search continues. Japanese authorities are involved in the effort to find the missing student.

cards.headline: Anthropic co-founder calls for ability to slow AI development
cards.teaser: A leading AI company executive warned that artificial intelligence could reach a point where it advances without human control.
cards.body:
Jack Clark, co-founder of AI company Anthropic, said regulators need the ability to slow down artificial intelligence development. Speaking on BBC's Newsnight, Clark warned that AI systems could eventually reach a stage where they develop independently of human input.

The comments reflect growing concerns within the tech industry about the rapid pace of AI advancement. Clark's position is notable given his role at one of the companies at the forefront of developing advanced AI systems.

cards.headline: Zelensky proposes direct talks with Putin to end war
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president sent an open letter to Russia's leader proposing face-to-face negotiations as the US shifts focus to Iran.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has written an open letter directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations. In the letter, Zelensky argues that only direct engagement between the two leaders can end the war. This marks the first public letter Zelensky has addressed directly to Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion began in 2022.

Zelensky has proposed meeting in a neutral third country to conduct talks. The letter includes a sweeping criticism of Putin's 26 years in power.

cards.headline: Putin pledges to strengthen air defenses after Ukrainian drone strikes
cards.teaser: Russia's president said his country will bolster air defenses following Ukrainian drone attacks that reached deep inside Russian territory.
cards.body:
President Vladimir Putin announced plans to strengthen Russia's air defense systems following recent Ukrainian drone attacks that have penetrated deep into Russian territory. The strikes disrupted Putin's economic forum in St. Petersburg, his hometown.

The drone operations demonstrate Ukraine's expanding capability to conduct long-range strikes inside Russia. Putin's pledge to bolster air defenses indicates concern about vulnerabilities in Russian airspace to Ukrainian operations.

cards.headline: Bitcoin drops near $62,000 as crypto markets decline
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency fell during its worst week in months as investor interest shifted away from digital assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped to near $62,000, approaching its 2026 low as the cryptocurrency market experienced a sharp decline. The digital asset weathered its most difficult week in months, with the token HYPE falling 14%.

The decline came as the so-called AI trade unwound and liquidity moved to other investments. Analysts noted that Bitcoin could fall further to $60,000, while other cryptocurrencies also posted significant losses. Zcash plunged 37% as the broader crypto market faced selling pressure.

cards.headline: SpaceX lines up retail investors for IPO allocation
cards.teaser: The rocket company plans to offer shares directly to individual investors in what could become the largest public offering ever.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing to allocate shares to retail investors as part of its initial public offering, according to reports. The company told banks it would not move from its $135-per-share IPO price, setting the stage for what would be the largest public offering in history.

Jamie Dimon is planning to personally pitch investors on the offering, underscoring the significance of the deal for Wall Street. Banks are preparing to collect substantial fees from the transaction. However, the company has been blocked from early entry into benchmark indexes, as S&P reaffirmed its existing rules requiring a seasoning period before newly public companies can be added.

cards.headline: Anthropic calls for coordinated plan to halt AI development if risks increase
cards.teaser: The AI company proposed that labs should have the ability to slow or pause development as artificial intelligence advances.
cards.body:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said the industry needs coordinated plans to halt AI development if risks rise to dangerous levels. Clark told BBC Newsnight that artificial intelligence could reach a point where it develops without human input, requiring safeguards to prevent uncontrolled advancement.

The company urged a global pause in AI development and called for what Clark described as a brake pedal for the technology. Anthropic said 80% of its new production code is now written by its Claude AI system, demonstrating the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence capabilities. The company flagged self-improvement in AI systems as a particular concern requiring industry-wide coordination.

cards.headline: China builds economic barriers as global tensions increase
cards.teaser: Beijing is implementing changes it says are necessary for national security, but the moves may complicate overseas growth for Chinese companies.
cards.body:
China is constructing economic fortifications in response to rising international tensions. Beijing characterized the measures as necessary for national security, implementing policies that could create barriers between Chinese businesses and global markets.

The changes may complicate efforts by Chinese companies to pursue growth opportunities outside the country. The economic restrictions come as geopolitical tensions affect trade relationships and investment flows between China and other major economies.

cards.headline: S&P denies early index entry for SpaceX and other large IPOs
cards.teaser: The index provider reaffirmed rules requiring a waiting period before newly public companies can join benchmark indexes.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

S&P will not change its rules to allow SpaceX into its benchmark index immediately after the company goes public. The index provider reaffirmed existing regulations that require a seasoning period before newly public companies can be added to major indexes.

The decision affects SpaceX and other large upcoming IPOs that had sought accelerated inclusion. Investors who track benchmark indexes will not be required to purchase shares immediately, despite the offering's massive size. The ruling provides a reality check for the highly anticipated public offering.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided is primarily about soccer, Amazon gaming strategy, and general SpaceX IPO interest—not about S&P's specific decision on index entry rules. The only relevant sources mentioned (Axios and Reuters headlines) are already reflected in the original card text. No new confirmed details are present to warrant a rewrite.

cards.headline: British Heart Foundation to close 150 charity shops
cards.teaser: The organization cited an exceptionally challenging trading environment as it plans significant store closures.
cards.body:
The British Heart Foundation announced plans to close 150 charity shops across the country. The organization said it is responding to an exceptionally challenging trading environment that has made operating the stores financially difficult.

The closures represent a significant reduction in the charity's retail footprint. The foundation operates shops that sell donated goods to raise funds for heart disease research and support programs.

hero.headline: Microsoft AI Chief Calls Anthropic Models Too Expensive
hero.body:
Microsoft's artificial intelligence chief stated that Anthropic's AI models are too expensive for widespread use, according to remarks made at the company's Build 2026 developer conference. The comments come as Microsoft continues to expand its own AI offerings and partnerships, including its longstanding investment in OpenAI. The statement highlights growing tensions in the AI industry over pricing structures and model accessibility.

The criticism arrives as Anthropic has been experiencing rapid growth. The company announced that its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up sharply from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025. Anthropic has positioned itself as a major competitor in the large language model market, offering what it describes as safer and more reliable AI systems. The company is preparing for an initial public offering.

Despite Microsoft's public criticism of Anthropic's pricing, the companies have significant business ties. Microsoft integrates Anthropic's AI tools into systems it provides to the US military and has joined other tech giants in supporting Anthropic's legal challenges against Pentagon decisions. In an amicus brief submitted to federal court, Microsoft argued that blocking Anthropic from government work would create serious disruption for suppliers whose products rely on the AI company's technology. Google, Amazon, Apple and OpenAI also signed onto the brief supporting Anthropic.

The Pentagon designated Anthropic as a supply-chain risk in response to failed contract negotiations over a $200 million deal to deploy Anthropic's AI on classified military systems. Anthropic had insisted its technology should not be used for mass surveillance of US citizens or to power autonomous lethal weapons. The company's leadership explained that Anthropic does not have confidence that its Claude model would function reliably or safely if used to support lethal autonomous warfare.

Microsoft used its Build 2026 conference to announce several AI-related initiatives, including Project Solara, an Android operating system designed for AI agents rather than traditional applications. The company also unveiled new tools for building AI applications using Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft databases. The conference focused on positioning Windows as a trusted platform for AI development.

The debate over AI model pricing has become increasingly significant as companies race to deploy artificial intelligence across their products and services. Higher costs for accessing advanced AI models can limit which businesses can afford to integrate them, potentially affecting the pace of AI adoption across different industries. Microsoft's own AI strategy has centered on making tools accessible to developers and enterprises through its Azure cloud platform.

The comments from Microsoft's AI leadership suggest the company may be steering customers toward its own AI solutions or those of partners like OpenAI, where Microsoft has invested billions of dollars. As competition intensifies in the AI sector, pricing and cost efficiency are becoming key differentiators alongside technical capabilities and model performance.

cards.headline: Anthropic Revenue Reaches $47 Billion Ahead of Planned IPO
cards.teaser: Anthropic announced its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May as the AI company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
Anthropic has experienced explosive growth, with annualized revenue reaching $47 billion in May—a dramatic jump from $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company is preparing for an initial public offering as it capitalizes on strong demand for its large language models.

Company president Daniela Amodei has addressed skepticism about returns on AI investments, expressing confidence as Anthropic navigates an increasingly competitive market and works to sustain its rapid growth trajectory.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky Plans to Launch AI Laboratory
cards.teaser: Airbnb's chief executive announced plans to establish a new artificial intelligence research lab.
cards.body:
Brian Chesky, Airbnb's CEO, plans to launch a new AI laboratory. The initiative reflects the company's commitment to developing artificial intelligence capabilities suited to its platform.

Last year, Chesky stated that Airbnb had not yet partnered with large language model providers because existing products did not meet the company's requirements. The new lab appears positioned to enable Airbnb to build customized AI solutions tailored to its specific needs and user experience.

cards.headline: Former OpenAI Executive Mira Murati Returns to Public View
cards.teaser: Mira Murati, who previously served in leadership at OpenAI, has re-emerged in the tech industry spotlight.
cards.body:
Mira Murati has stepped back into public view after keeping a lower profile following her time at OpenAI. Industry observers note that in the current competitive environment for AI talent and startups, maintaining visibility has become increasingly important for attracting attention and investment.

Murati's return to public activity comes at a time when former executives from major AI companies are launching new ventures and competing for funding. The approach reflects a shift in strategy, with observers noting that remaining out of sight has diminishing returns when building market presence.

cards.headline: Founders Fund Launches Game Show Featuring Tech Industry Leaders
cards.teaser: Investment firm Founders Fund premiered a game show starring prominent technology executives and entrepreneurs.
cards.body:
Founders Fund, a prominent venture capital firm, has launched a game show featuring prominent technology industry figures. The debut episode was moderated by Mike Solana, Founders Fund's chief marketing officer, and included a cast of current tech luminaries such as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anduril founder Palmer Luckey.

The show represents a new format for the venture capital firm to engage with and showcase personalities from the technology sector.

cards.headline: Researchers Identify East Asia's Tallest Tree After Decade-Long Search
cards.teaser: Scientists have crowned a Taiwania cryptomerioides nicknamed 'The Heaven Sword' as the tallest tree in East Asia.
cards.body:
A tree known as 'The Heaven Sword' has been identified as the tallest in East Asia after a search spanning nearly a decade. The Taiwania cryptomerioides stands 80 meters tall, according to measurements by researchers.

The discovery required years of systematic searching and verification by scientists working to catalog exceptional trees across the region. The tree's height makes it a significant botanical finding, providing insight into the maximum growth potential of the species in East Asian forests.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 to Use Both Exynos and Snapdragon Processors
cards.teaser: Samsung will equip its upcoming Galaxy Z Flip8 with both Exynos and Snapdragon chipsets in different markets.
cards.body:
Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip8 will feature both Exynos and Snapdragon processors depending on the region, according to industry reports. The dual-chip strategy mirrors the approach Samsung has used for its Galaxy S series flagship phones.

The decision brings back Snapdragon chips to the Z Flip line alongside Samsung's own Exynos processors. The strategy appears aimed at managing production costs while maintaining performance across different markets, though it has historically drawn criticism from consumers who prefer one chipset over the other.

hero.headline: Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge out at least four weeks with rib stress fracture
hero.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has been diagnosed with a stress fracture in his rib on his right side and will be reevaluated in four to six weeks. The injury represents a significant setback for the Yankees as they navigate the 2026 season without one of baseball's premier power hitters.

Judge's absence leaves a substantial void in the Yankees lineup. The team now faces at least a month without their star player, who has been a cornerstone of the franchise in recent years. The Yankees will need to adjust their roster and batting order to compensate for the loss during his recovery period.

Stress fractures in ribs typically require rest and limited physical activity to heal properly. The four to six week timeline means Judge will miss a considerable portion of the season, though the exact duration depends on how his body responds to treatment. The Yankees medical staff will monitor his progress closely before determining when he can resume baseball activities.

The injury comes at a time when the Yankees are trying to position themselves in the competitive American League standings. Judge's production both at the plate and in the outfield has been integral to the team's success. His power hitting and defensive capabilities make him one of the most valuable players in the league.

The Yankees organization now faces decisions about how to fill the roster spot and whether any roster moves or adjustments will be necessary during Judge's absence. The team will rely on other players to step up offensively while awaiting his return to full health.

cards.headline: Hurricanes defeat Golden Knights in Game 2 to tie Stanley Cup Final at one game each
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes evened the Stanley Cup Final series with a Game 2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights.
cards.body:
Seth Jarvis scored the overtime winner on a power play as the Carolina Hurricanes rallied to beat the Vegas Golden Knights 4-3 in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final. The Hurricanes erased a two-goal third-period deficit in a thrilling final frame that saw four goals scored. A failed Vegas challenge resulted in the crucial power play that set up Jarvis's game-winning goal at 3:56 of overtime.

The victory evens the series at one game apiece after Vegas won the opener. Carolina's comeback in regulation, followed by Jarvis's heroics in OT, gives the Hurricanes momentum as the series continues.

cards.headline: Lynx guard Olivia Miles breaks WNBA rookie three-point record
cards.teaser: Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles set a new WNBA record for three-pointers by a first-year player.
cards.body:
Olivia Miles made eight three-pointers in the Minnesota Lynx victory over Golden State, breaking the previous WNBA rookie record held by Caitlin Clark. The performance helped lead the Lynx to an 87-84 win over the Golden State franchise.

Miles has moved to the front of the pack in WNBA rookie rankings following her record-setting performance. The guard's shooting performance marks a milestone in her first professional season and establishes her as one of the top rookies in the league.

cards.headline: Jennifer Kupcho leads US Women's Open after first round
cards.teaser: Jennifer Kupcho holds a one-shot lead following the opening round of the US Women's Open golf tournament.
cards.body:
Jennifer Kupcho made an impressive start to the US Women's Open, golf's second women's major of the year. After the first round on Thursday, she holds a one-shot lead at the top of the leaderboard.

With strong opening round performance behind her, Kupcho is well-positioned as the tournament progresses into its remaining rounds.

cards.headline: Ireland extends rugby coach Andy Farrell's contract through 2031
cards.teaser: Andy Farrell signed a new contract with the Irish Rugby Football Union extending his tenure as Ireland men's head coach.
cards.body:
Ireland men's head coach Andy Farrell has signed a new contract with the Irish Rugby Football Union that will keep him in the role until 2031. The agreement extends Farrell's tenure leading the Irish national team for several more years.

The contract extension provides continuity for the Ireland rugby program. Farrell will continue to guide the team through upcoming international competitions and tournaments over the next several years under the terms of the new agreement.

cards.headline: Knicks prepare for Game 2 of NBA Finals against Spurs
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks are ready to face what they expect will be a more aggressive San Antonio team in the second game of the Finals.
cards.body:
The Knicks anticipate facing a more desperate Spurs team in Game 2 of the NBA Finals following New York's Game 1 victory. Josh Hart's contributions in the series opener went beyond scoring, demonstrating his versatility and impact on the game through multiple facets of play.

Hart matched a Larry Bird NBA Finals record with his all-around performance in Game 1. His ability to impact the game without relying solely on scoring has been a key factor for the Knicks as they compete for the championship.

cards.headline: French Open men's semifinals set with four first-time Grand Slam finalists
cards.teaser: The French Open will crown a first-time Grand Slam men's champion as all four semifinalists seek their maiden major title.
cards.body:
A first-time Grand Slam men's champion will be crowned at the French Open, as all four semifinalists are competing for their maiden major title. This ensures a historic final regardless of which players advance from the semifinals in Paris.

The mental challenge of handling the pressure will be crucial in determining who reaches the final. Each semifinalist must cope with the unique demands of competing for a first Grand Slam championship, with composure potentially separating the finalists from those eliminated.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Stabbed to Death in Los Angeles
hero.body:
Veteran actor James Handy, 81, died following a stabbing at his home in the Tarzana neighborhood of Los Angeles. Police discovered Handy unconscious in the front yard of his residence at 9:30am on Wednesday with multiple stab wounds to the chest.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested at the scene and has been charged on suspicion of murder. Bail was set at $2 million. According to the Los Angeles Police Department, a 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." Police noted that the suspect lives at the residence with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

Handy had a long career in entertainment spanning multiple decades. He was born in New York City and began his acting work in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. He became known for character roles in films including Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick, which was released in 2022. His television credits included appearances on Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. He also appeared in the films Logan and K-911.

The Los Angeles Police Department is continuing to investigate the circumstances of the incident. Authorities have not disclosed additional details about what preceded the fatal encounter or the nature of the relationship between Handy and the suspect beyond the fact that Gledhill is the son of Handy's girlfriend.

Handy's death has prompted tributes from his colleagues and fans, who have shared memories of his work on social media. The actor was a consistent presence in supporting roles throughout his career, contributing to numerous productions across film and television over his five decades in the industry.

The suspect remains in police custody as the case proceeds through the legal system. Additional charges may be forthcoming as the investigation develops. The case adds to concerns about violent incidents affecting people in the Los Angeles area in recent times.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Earns $7.5 Million in Thursday Previews
cards.teaser: The horror comedy sequel matched Scream 7 levels in preview screenings, while Masters of the Universe took in $4 million.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie installment earned $7.5 million in Thursday night preview screenings, approaching the performance of Scream 7 during its preview period. The horror comedy franchise returns after a hiatus with this latest entry.

Masters of the Universe collected $4 million in Thursday previews. The Scary Movie series has historically relied on timing, capitalizing on trends in horror films. The sixth installment aims to spoof current horror movies and other genres, continuing the franchise's tradition of broad parody humor.

cards.headline: Steve Lacy Announces Third Album With New Single
cards.teaser: The musician released a new lovelorn single titled The Feeling ahead of his album Oh Yeah? arriving in July.
cards.body:
Steve Lacy has announced his third studio album, Oh Yeah?, arriving in July. He's shared the lead single "The Feeling," a lovelorn track that marks his return with new material.

The musician continues to build on his success as both a solo artist and member of the band The Internet. "The Feeling" offers the first taste of what's to come on the upcoming album.

cards.headline: Tinashe Releases New Single Too Easy
cards.teaser: The singer dropped a new track that she first previewed during her DJ set at Coachella earlier this year.
cards.body:
Tinashe released a new single titled Too Easy, a track she previously teased during her performance at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival. The song showcases a confident, swaggering style.

The singer performed a DJ set at Coachella earlier in 2026, where she gave audiences their first listen to the new material. Tinashe has been releasing music independently in recent years, building a dedicated fan base through her consistent output and live performances.

cards.headline: Phoebe Bridgers Performs Eight New Songs at Phone-Free Madison Square Garden Show
cards.teaser: The singer-songwriter played an intimate acoustic concert for 18,000 fans who agreed to lock up their phones for the performance.
cards.body:
Phoebe Bridgers held a special acoustic concert at Madison Square Garden where approximately 18,000 attendees were required to lock away their phones for the entire show. During the intimate performance, she debuted eight new songs and addressed the audience about the phone-free format, expressing her appreciation for the internet-free environment.

The acoustic setup created a personal atmosphere despite the large venue size, marking a significant departure from typical arena concert experiences. Bridgers told the crowd how much she valued the phone-free approach, thanking fans for embracing this unusual concert format.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Contributes Song to Toy Story 5
cards.teaser: Swift co-wrote and produced a heartfelt track about Jessie with longtime collaborator Jack Antonoff.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift co-wrote and produced a new song for Toy Story 5 titled "I Knew It, I Knew You," collaborating with longtime producer Jack Antonoff. The heartfelt track centers on the character Jessie.

The film continues the adventures of Woody, Buzz, and other beloved Pixar characters. According to actor Tom Hanks, the latest installment explores themes around children's screen addiction, with the toys competing for attention against a tablet.

cards.headline: Florida Georgia Line Reunite at CMA Fest
cards.teaser: Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley made a surprise appearance together at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, signaling the return of the duo.
cards.body:
Florida Georgia Line reunited with an unexpected performance at CMA Fest in Nashville. Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley appeared together at Nissan Stadium, marking their first joint performance since splitting in 2022.

The duo's surprise appearance signals a potential return for Florida Georgia Line after a four-year hiatus. Hubbard and Kelley had pursued separate solo projects following their split. CMA Fest is one of country music's major annual events, drawing large crowds to Nashville.

hero.headline: Senate passes $69.5 billion immigration enforcement funding package
hero.body:
The Senate voted early Friday morning to pass a $69.5 billion budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement operations through 2029. The legislation passed 52-47 following an overnight session that included contentious debates over amendments.

The bill represents a significant expansion of resources for immigration enforcement and border security operations over the next three years. The measure now moves to the House for final passage before President Donald Trump can sign it into law.

The contentious debate centered on a proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund that the Trump administration intends to create to compensate political allies who claim they were prosecuted by the Biden-era Justice Department. Several Republicans objected to the fund and worked to block it through amendments.

During the marathon voting session, six Republican senators broke ranks with their party to support an amendment sponsored by Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana designed to block the fund. Those senators included Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Dan Sullivan of Alaska, and Joni Ernst of Iowa.

Cassidy spent considerable time during the overnight session perfecting the language of his amendment to prevent the administration from establishing the compensation fund. He consulted with Senate Parliamentarian Elizabeth MacDonough to ensure the amendment could withstand procedural challenges.

The division revealed internal Republican disagreements over spending priorities and the anti-weaponization fund, yet party leadership maintained sufficient support for passage. Despite the splits, Republicans held together enough votes to pass the measure without Democratic support.

The funding package comes amid broader debates over immigration enforcement and departmental operations. Democrats had previously blocked a separate Department of Homeland Security funding bill, demanding reforms to Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. Those proposed changes included requirements that agents wear identification and body cameras, as well as restrictions preventing them from operating near schools, medical facilities, churches, polling stations, childcare facilities, and courts.

Democrats also sought guarantees that local and state law enforcement agencies could investigate potential crimes committed by federal authorities, including excessive use of force. Republicans supported body cameras but resisted other proposals, arguing they would restrict agents' ability to conduct operations effectively.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer stated his party wanted "commonsense" changes in how immigration enforcement operates. "From day one, I've said unless there were really strong, meaningful reforms to rein in ICE and stop the violence, there will not be Democratic votes to fund ICE," Schumer said.

Republican leaders expressed confidence the House will pass the measure in coming days. The bill's passage represents a victory for Republican leadership despite the internal tensions revealed during the overnight voting marathon and amendments debate.

cards.headline: House Armed Services Committee advances $1.15 trillion defense bill
cards.teaser: The committee passed the annual defense policy bill after debating hundreds of amendments for 14 hours.
cards.body:
The House Armed Services Committee approved the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act on Thursday, advancing the $1.15 trillion defense policy bill to the full House for consideration.

The committee voted 44 in favor of the measure after spending 14 hours debating approximately 900 proposed amendments. The annual defense authorization bill now awaits action by the full chamber.

cards.headline: Trump pushes Congress to make daylight saving time permanent
cards.teaser: The president is personally calling lawmakers to lobby for ending the twice-yearly clock changes.
cards.body:
President Trump is personally calling lawmakers to support legislation that would make daylight saving time permanent across the United States. The push would eliminate the twice-yearly clock changes that have been standard practice for decades.

This initiative is one of several personal priorities Trump is advancing that are testing Republican support in Congress, reflecting his individual agenda over traditional party positions.

cards.headline: Former Biden Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The victory positions her to potentially make history in the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously served as a member of Congress representing New Mexico before joining the Biden cabinet.

cards.headline: Katie Porter, Steve Hilton lead early returns in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Multiple candidates from both parties are competing to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Early results show Steve Hilton leading Republican candidates and Katie Porter among top Democratic contenders in California's gubernatorial primary. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing for their party's nomination, while Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton vie for theirs.

The race will determine who replaces Governor Gavin Newsom, who is not seeking reelection. California's primary system allows the top two vote-getters regardless of party to advance to the general election.

cards.headline: House members struggle in campaigns for higher office
cards.teaser: Multiple members of Congress have lost recent bids for Senate seats and governorships.
cards.body: House members have faced repeated defeats in their bids for higher office, including Senate and gubernatorial races. Analysts point to Congress's low public approval ratings as a key factor, with voters appearing unwilling to promote members of an institution they view as unpopular and dysfunctional. This pattern has sparked debate among political strategists about whether a House career has become a disadvantage for candidates seeking statewide positions.

cards.headline: Republican pollster analyzes voter sentiment on Trump agenda
cards.teaser: Jim Hobart discusses how key Trump initiatives are shaping midterm voter decisions.
cards.body:
Republican pollster Jim Hobart provided analysis on how voters view President Trump's agenda, including the Iran conflict, the proposed anti-weaponization fund, and other administration priorities. The assessment examines what factors are influencing voter choices ahead of midterm elections.

The analysis comes as Trump pursues several initiatives that have divided Republicans in Congress. Hobart's polling work focuses on understanding how these policy debates translate into voter behavior and what drives midterm election decisions.
